html:
The Mordvins are a people of the middle Volga region of Russia, between the Oka and the Sura rivers. They are really two peoples, the Erzya and the Moksha, who speak two related languages of the Uralic family. The map shows them around 800.

They lived by farming, hunting, fishing and beekeeping in the forests. The Gothic historian Jordanes may name them as the Mordens in the 500s. In the Middle Ages they traded with the Volga Bulgars and with Rus princes, who fought them for land.

They came under the Golden Horde in the 1200s and under Moscow after it took Kazan in 1552. Russian peasants moved into their lands, and the Orthodox Church baptised most of them in the 1700s. Many Mordvins have since adopted Russian, but Mordovia remains a republic of Russia.
